target.title: fix(config): restore env changes before rethrowing INVALID_CONFIG
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadConfigLocal()` applies `env.vars` to `process.env` during config resolution via `resolveConfigForRead()` → `applyConfigEnvVars()`. When config validation fails with `INVALID_CONFIG`, the catch block at line 1942 rethrows without restoring the env snapshot, leaking env side effects into the running process.

**Trigger**: An `openclaw.json` with valid `env.vars` entries but other invalid config sections. Running `openclaw doctor` on such a config would leave `process.env` polluted with the vars from the invalid config.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three other code paths in the same file already follow the correct pattern of calling `restoreEnvChangesIfUnchanged()` before returning/retrying after config operations that modify env:

| Location | Scenario |
|---|---|
| Line 1906 | `loadConfigLocal()` — retry after suspicious recovery |
| Line 2169 | `readConfigFileSnapshotInternal()` — retry after suspicious recovery |
| Line 3242 | `writeAndActivateConfig()` — rollback after write failure |

The `INVALID_CONFIG` path was the only one missing this cleanup.

## User Impact

- Before: invalid config with `env.vars` → env leaked → subsequent operations see wrong env values
- After: env is properly restored before rethrowing, matching the behavior of all other error/retry paths

## Evidence

- Static analysis: `grep -n restoreEnvChangesIfUnchanged src/config/io.ts` confirms 3 existing call sites at lines 1906, 2169, 3242, all following the same snapshot-before / snapshot-after / restore pattern around lines 1778-1909
- `restoreEnvChangesIfUnchanged()` (line 1403) is safe/stable: only restores keys where `env[key] === after[key]`, meaning it won't clobber external env mutations
